note: Hebrew has simply wesheba "and Sheba"; the KJV reads it as an alternative name for Beersheba to fit the total of thirteen cities in v.6 (LXX reads Shema, cf. 15:26).
Hammeto'ar is a participle "that bends/is marked out" describing the boundary's course to Neah; the KJV makes it part of a compound place name.
The Hebrew is Ebron ('Evron, with ayin), a town in Asher, not the Judean Hebron (Chevron); the KJV spelling confuses the two (many MSS read Abdon, cf. 21:30).

kjv: from Allon to Zaanannim, and Adami, Nekeb
mine: from the oak at Zaanannim, and Adami-nekeb
note: Me'elon betsa'anannim is "from the oak (terebinth) in Zaanannim" (cf. Judg 4:11); Adami-hanneqeb is likely a single place name.

kjv: went out [too little] for them (the people of Dan)
mine: slipped from them (the people of Dan)
note: Wayyetse gebul ... mehem "the territory went out from them" means it was lost to them (cf. Judg 1:34); the KJV supplies "too little" to make it mean their territory was too small.
